lens: Apple-inspired clarity — first encounter (simulated expert reviewer)
reason: The inspected public experience has strong hierarchy and a coherent Precision Instrument identity. The desktop hero clearly distinguishes its two audience actions, while the mobile capture preserves readable sections, generous spacing and a deliberate single-column sequence. The engagement bench expresses the engineering identity through a useful process explanation: selected controls have pressed state, the readout announces changes, and reduced motion removes its transition. I traced the client journey from proposition and engagement terms to the inquiry form and its acknowledgement. The supplied browser test exercises that journey but intercepts the contact API; it establishes local interface behavior rather than successful delivery to the board. The form provides a sending state, errors and an email fallback, and its API only returns normal success after the email helper reports delivery. Factual restraint is credible: the homepage explicitly marks pending case-study approval instead of inventing outcomes, and application materials accurately disclose original-resume visibility. These are strong local design qualities. They do not establish a world-class end-to-end website across application, grading and operator workflows: those broader tasks were not independently exercised by this seat, hosted integrations remain untested, and no human task-success evidence exists. My verdict is therefore unproven rather than conditional agreement.

findings.evidence: The first-view proposition says 'Student-led consulting' and describes recommendations, but omits cost. 'Pro bono' first appears through SEMESTER_FACTS in the later process section (home/page.tsx:100-108; src/lib/site-content.ts:158-163). The supplied desktop-hero.png shows neither a cost statement nor a clear eligibility statement.
findings.userImpact: An organization assessing fit at first encounter must continue scanning to discover the unusually relevant fact that MECG does not charge a consulting fee.
findings.suggestedFix: Include 'pro bono' or 'no consulting fee' in the existing hero supporting sentence, retaining the current two actions and typography.

notVerified: No staging or hosted acceptance exists; actual Clerk sessions, Supabase/RLS, storage and email delivery were not verified.
Application, grading, decision release and owner operations were not independently exercised by this seat; receipt claims are not observed user success.
No human usability study, assistive-technology session, physical-device, Safari or Firefox validation was supplied.
Client-approved project outcomes and artifacts remain absent; no outcome claim or approval was inferred.
